title: Everyday Choices and Clear Plans
subtitle: A practical revision pack for weather, quantities, comparisons, and useful work messages.

days.title: Day 1 — Describe the situation clearly
days.intro: Use impersonal it and quantity phrases in everyday updates.

activities.title: Practical messages
activities.instructions: Read the examples and make one message about your day.
activities.content: It is raining. It is nearly six o’clock. We have a few questions and a little time.

activities.title: Plan around real conditions
activities.instructions: Choose the reply that fits the situation.
activities.content: Use it for weather, time, distance, and general situations. Use a few with countable plural nouns and a little with uncountable nouns.

questions.prompt: Your train is delayed. Which update fits?
options: It is running ten minutes late.
There is running ten minutes late.

questions.prompt: You are preparing drinks. Which note fits?
options: We have a little water left.
We have a few water left.

activities.title: A rainy commute
activities.instructions: Read both roles and make the time or route your own.

dialogue.speaker: Mina
dialogue.text: Is it still raining near you?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes, but it should stop soon.

dialogue.speaker: Mina
dialogue.text: Do we have a little more time?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s leave ten minutes later.

patterns: Do we have a little more time?

days.title: Day 2 — Make a useful choice
days.intro: Compare routes, suppliers, and plans clearly.

activities.title: Choose the best route
activities.instructions: Read the route note aloud, then compare two routes you know.
activities.content: The side streets are quieter than the bridge road. This is the best route when there is heavy traffic.

activities.title: A client visit
activities.instructions: Read the plan and choose the detail that answers each question.
activities.content: The main road is shorter, but the side streets are quieter. The team chooses the shortcut because it is the most reliable route when traffic is heavy.

questions.prompt: Why does the team choose the shortcut?
options: It is the most reliable in heavy traffic.
It is always the shortest route.
It is next to the supplier.

activities.title: Weather and travel
activities.instructions: Listen to the external forecast, then answer the questions on the platform.
activities.content: Listen for changes in weather and decide what they mean for a travel plan.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: The local supplier is faster than the other one.

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: Which option is best for our budget?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: The smaller order is the best value this week.

days.title: Day 3 — Write and say practical plans
days.intro: Use the new language in a clear workplace message.

activities.title: Plan a client visit
activities.instructions: Write 5–7 sentences for a colleague. Mention weather or time, one amount, and the best route or choice. This written work is for review.
activities.content: Useful starters: It is… We have a few… There is a little… This is better than… It is the best…

activities.title: Explain a practical choice
activities.instructions: Say four short sentences aloud. Include one sentence with it, one quantity phrase, and two comparisons.

activities.title: Before the visit
activities.instructions: Read both roles, then make the details your own.

dialogue.speaker: Emre
dialogue.text: Yes, but it is lighter now.

dialogue.speaker: Emre
dialogue.text: The side street is quieter and more reliable.
